debt.title: a canon sync that finds same-id-different-text renumbers silently instead of surfacing the conflict
debt.why: Renumbering is right for two people colliding on a number and wrong for one decision that was edited — it orphans every existing reference to that id. Every attempt to reconcile from the tool produced a third copy. Surface both and ask; if a renumber really is the default, rewrite the references in the same transaction or say which ones are now stale.
debt.drop_reason: phase 18 removed the failure mode instead of reporting it: mergeDecisions now refuses a same-id/different-content collision and names both entries, and nothing is ever renumbered (ADR-053 D5, pinned by tests/canon.test.mjs against a real bare remote)

debt.title: ac canon push publishes CONVENTIONS.md only, so an edit to an existing ADR never reaches the registry
debt.why: canonPush guards on p.conventions alone and ac decision add is the sole publisher of DECISIONS.md. Editing a published ADR leaves the registry stale; the next sync sees same-id-different-text, keeps both and renumbers one, producing one decision under two ids with the richer copy carrying the number nothing references. Observed end to end 2026-09-12.
debt.drop_reason: phase 18 closed it by refusal rather than by bulk-pushing an append-only log: an edit to an already-published decision is detected and refused with supersession named as the supported path (ADR-053 D4), so the edit no longer needs to reach the registry to avoid being lost

debt.title: ac install uses symlinkSync with no copy fallback, so a standard Windows user gets EPERM
debt.why: lib/install.mjs:81 symlinks unconditionally; on Windows symlinks need Developer Mode or an elevated shell, so a normal install fails. A copy fallback must keep REQ-008 reversibility — uninstall has to recognise copies too. Flagged 2026-06-12 by the first external install attempt; item 1 of that report (the PowerShell 'ac' alias) was fixed, this one never was.

debt.title: ac phase add and ac phase note strip the planned flag from every line of ROADMAP.md
debt.why: Both re-render with renderRoadmapMd(rm) on the raw roadmap.json, but planned is disk-derived and only renderRoadmap(root) computes it from each phase's PLAN.md. Cosmetic and self-healing on the next render, which is why it has survived — but ac phase add runs on every fleet run that claims a phase, so it re-strips constantly and shows a diff nobody asked for. Fix is one word in each place.

debt.title: nothing publishes CONVENTIONS.md when a phase closes, so the next ac canon pull silently reverts local edits
debt.why: A phase whose tasks edit .astrocode/CONVENTIONS.md leaves the registry stale, and the pull that /astro-plan and /astro-execute both run overwrites the local file while printing success. Observed: a raised Go core ceiling reverted under a tracked line count that had already passed it. ADR-041 states the discipline as a rule humans must remember, which is the tell that the tool should just do it.
debt.drop_reason: phase 18 closed both ends: ac decision add now publishes a locally-edited CONVENTIONS.md (ADR-053 D3) and a pull refuses to overwrite a diverged copy instead of silently reverting it (D1); the implicit publish itself refuses when it would delete a teammate newer published copy

debt.title: the planner has no guidance for test-first task pairs split across a wave boundary
debt.why: An ESM import of a not-yet-existing export fails the whole test file, so 'write failing tests' is structurally impossible without stubs — which pushes the test task's executor to implement, overflowing its declared files and breaking the wave's file-disjointness. That was cause 2 of the phase-04 wave-2 incident. The other four bullets from that report shipped (heal ladder, fork-base guard under ADR-040, file-ownership enforcement, ADR-017 stamped resumability); this one did not.

debt.title: ac milestone new never persists the bumped milestone number to roadmap.json
debt.why: bin/ac.mjs mutates the object returned by loadRoadmap() and then calls renderRoadmap(), which re-reads from disk (lib/roadmap.mjs:118-119) and discards the mutation. state.active_milestone bumps correctly but roadmap.json.milestone stays on the OLD number, so ac status and the generated ROADMAP.md both report the previous milestone. Worse, completeMilestone reads rm.milestone to pick the archive directory — so completing the new milestone would archive its phases into the PREVIOUS milestone's archive dir, merging two unrelated milestones (m7 phases would land in .astrocode/milestones/6/ next to the already-archived phases 11-15). Observed live on 2026-09-19: ac milestone new claimed 7, state went to 7, roadmap.json stayed at 6. flowBranch is unaffected because it prefers state.active_milestone.
debt.drop_reason: fixed on 2026-09-20 in 4da9f05 — ac milestone new now calls setMilestone(r, res.number) alongside updateState, so the bumped number reaches roadmap.json (bin/ac.mjs:587). Verified at v0.24.1 during the phase-20 discuss.

debt.why: `git worktree list` shows .claude/worktrees/wf_7e0f9d53-f43-10 and wf_e41e92cd-a11-5 still registered, with branches worktree-wf_7e0f9d53-f43-10 and worktree-wf_e41e92cd-a11-5. debt.title: a canon sync that finds same-id-different-text renumbers silently instead of surfacing the conflict
debt.why: RE-FILED 2026-09-20: dropped by a phase-18 remediation cycle, then reproduced by that same run's verifier. Worse than originally described — lib/decisions.mjs:46 parseDecisions keys by id and src.match() resolves to the FIRST occurrence, so a second entry under the same id is invisible to mergeDecisions and is silently DESTROYED when merged text is written (verifier C5: bob's hand-written '## ADR-001 — Ban worktrees' gone after pull, grep -c = 0, plain success reported). A project that already holds duplicate ids is exactly the input that triggers it.
debt.drop_reason: Fixed in phase 18 and independently re-driven by the verifier on 2026-09-20: the same-id case now refuses with the file byte-unchanged (pull prints '⚠ DECISIONS.md: refused' naming both titles; grep -c 'Ban worktrees' = 1, not 0). parseDecisionEntries sees every entry and the merge refuses on a duplicate id instead of discarding a side. Probed neighbours too — two local same-id entries, a registry-side duplicate id, a same-id exact duplicate — no residual silent drop.

debt.title: a decisions-collision refusal prints a malformed empty fix list: 'Fix: .'
debt.why: lib/canon.mjs:356 builds the DECISIONS.md refusal with `fixes: []`, so every same-id collision — pull and decision add alike — prints the dangling sentence '⚠ DECISIONS.md was NOT overwritten — a same-id decision collision was found. Fix: .' The CONVENTIONS.md refusal a few lines down does carry a real list and reads correctly, which is what makes the empty one look like a bug to a reader. No criterion is harmed: the following line names both colliding decisions and states supersession. Fix is to populate the list with the supported route (record a superseding decision) or omit the sentence when there are no fixes.

debt.title: ac canon push publishes CONVENTIONS.md only, so an edit to an existing ADR never reaches the registry
debt.why: RE-FILED 2026-09-20: dropped by a phase-18 remediation cycle while still reproducible. Retained as originally filed on 2026-09-17.
debt.drop_reason: Closed by design rather than by code: an edit to a published ADR deliberately does NOT reach the registry. ADR-053 makes published decisions immutable — editing one is refused with supersession explained (verified as C6: 'refused — ADR-001 was edited locally after publishing'). Propagating such an edit is now the wrong behaviour, so the gap this named is closed, not outstanding. Dropped rather than dismissed: it was a genuine gap when filed on 2026-09-17, before that decision existed.

debt.title: canon pull silently deletes hand-written non-ADR prose from DECISIONS.md and reports plain success
debt.why: Observed directly: appending a hand-written non-ADR paragraph to DECISIONS.md and running `ac canon pull` left grep -c = 0, with the pull printing only '✓ DECISIONS.md: updated from astro-registry'. mergeDecisions rebuilds the file as remoteText plus entries recognised by the ^##\s+(ADR-\d+) heading scan, so anything outside a heading block is dropped. Outside all ten criteria — they identify a decision by its heading throughout — and partly inherent, since the local preamble is replaced by the registry's on every pull, which is the mirror semantics convergence requires. Filed because the phase goal's 'never silently destroy local canon' extends past ADR blocks, and free prose is indistinguishable from the preamble to the merge. A warning naming the discarded text would be enough.

debt.title: nothing publishes CONVENTIONS.md when a phase closes, so the next ac canon pull silently reverts local edits
debt.why: RE-FILED 2026-09-20: dropped by a phase-18 remediation cycle, then reproduced by that same run's verifier as C7. The D3 implicit publish is gated on registryMoved (lib/canon.mjs:132), which requires synced != null — any copy that has never run canon pull/push has no baseline, so the publish fires unconditionally and overwrites a teammate's published copy with no warning. .astrocode/.conventions-synced is untracked AND not gitignored, so every fresh clone starts in that unguarded branch.
debt.drop_reason: Fixed in phase 18 and independently re-driven on 2026-09-20: ac decision add now publishes a locally-edited CONVENTIONS.md, and refuses rather than clobbering in BOTH shapes — baseline-present-and-registry-moved, and never-synced-at-all. .astrocode/.conventions-synced is gitignored, so a fresh clone no longer starts in the unguarded branch. Verifier observed the teammate's line surviving in the registry in each probe.

debt.title: ac backlog list says "oldest first" but sorts by id, so same-day captures list out of capture order
debt.why: The sort is lexicographic on the date-prefixed id, so within a single day it is slug order, not age order. Observed in a scratch project: an item captured at 13:36:58.851 listed after one captured at 13:36:58.900. The --help line 'open ideas (oldest first)' is inaccurate for the common case of several ideas captured in one session, and the 0d age column makes the ordering look authoritative. Either sort on captured_at or soften the help text.

debt.title: The statusline hook crashes with an unhandled EPIPE when its stdout reader closes early
debt.why: Piping the hook into a short consumer (node hooks/astro-statusline.mjs < payload | head -3) makes the final process.stdout.write throw an uncaught 'Error: write EPIPE', printing a Node stack trace to stderr and exiting non-zero. Claude Code captures stdout in full so this is not a live-user path, which is why no criterion touches it — but it makes the hook unpleasant to debug by hand, and any future caller that pipes it sees a stack trace instead of a truncated line. A try/catch or an EPIPE listener around the final write would close it.
